review_notes: I read the whole file and the ConstraintGraph simp lemmas (head_reverse, edgeSatisfied_reverse). I grepped the repository for downstream uses of the InitialGraph definitions. The other files only use the cardinality and gap theorems, plus raw and raw_satisfiable_iff. The simp interface for the vertex-level definitions is the weakest point: honestLabeling is not reachable by simp without unfolding the vertex constructors. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that simp fails or loops. The card_* simp lemmas look fine. card_label is probably redundant with the existing Fintype.card_prod and Fintype.card_bool simp lemmas, but I judged that too minor to report.

simp [incidenceAccept, honestLabeling, clauseVertex, variableVertex, variableLabel,
    variableValid, honest_satisfies, honest_answerAt, hc]
findings.problem: honestLabeling is defined by matching on `.inl (.inl v)` and `.inl (.inr i)`, but every user-facing statement goes through the opaque defs `variableVertex` and `clauseVertex`. The file has no simp equations for `honestLabeling F A (variableVertex F v)` or `honestLabeling F A (clauseVertex F i)`. The only simp proof of the honest-labeling fact (incidence_honest) must therefore unfold the vertex constructors and the Label helpers by hand. The same unfolding would be needed in any other proof about honest labelings. The file also has no simp lemmas for `tail F` on `.inl (event, false/true)`, and the `raw_forward` identity (not tagged simp) covers only the forward orientation. Unfolding `clauseVertex`/`variableVertex` exposes raw `Sum.inl (Sum.inl _)` terms. That breaks the intended normal form `variableVertex F v` / `clauseVertex F i` and makes the simp call depend on the encoding of Vertex.
findings.proposed_change:
Add simp equation lemmas stated at the named-vertex level, for example:
`@[simp] theorem honestLabeling_variableVertex (F) (A) (v) : honestLabeling F A (variableVertex F v) = variableLabel (A v) := rfl`
`@[simp] theorem honestLabeling_clauseVertex (F) (A) (i) : honestLabeling F A (clauseVertex F i) = fromClauseAnswer (honestAnswer (clauseAt F i) A) := rfl`
Also add `@[simp] tail_forward` and `tail_backward` lemmas for `tail F (.inl (event, false/true))`. Then reduce the proof of incidence_honest to `simp [incidenceAccept, variableLabel, variableValid, honest_satisfies, honest_answerAt, hc]`, with no vertex defs unfolded. The alternative is to mark `variableVertex` and `clauseVertex` as `abbrev` or `@[reducible]`, but the explicit equation lemmas keep the normal form stable.
findings.benefit: Simp proofs about honest labelings and edge satisfaction stay at the level of `variableVertex`/`clauseVertex`. They no longer depend on the `Sum` encoding of Vertex, and new proofs can reuse the lemmas without repeating the unfolding list. The simp set also gets a canonical form for vertices instead of an ad hoc `simp [defs…]` call.
